title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, i.e. how the Deligne–Mumford boundary looks near each stratum. The local model is X = C^I with the normal-crossings divisor Σ z_i = 0. In the previous page's notation (P apparently stands for the origin/point factor):
- D_J = P^J × C^{I\J} is the closed stratum {z_i = 0 for i in J}, of codimension card J.
- D*_J = P^J × C*^{I\J} is the open stratum where z_i = 0 exactly for i in J.
The 'elementary topos' under study is built from a partition I = I'_0 ⊔ I'_1 ⊔ I''. Its 'âme' (soul) has dimension card I'_1.

This page.
- (271): the soul is A = D*_{I\I'_1}, the open stratum indexed by I'_0 ⊔ I''. It sits inside the closure of R = D*_{I'_0} (the bar D_{I'_0}) as an immersion of codimension card I''. So A is a deeper stratum in the closure of R.
- The index set I'' further splits as I''_0 ⊔ I''_*.
- If I'' = I''_0, the topos is the tubular neighbourhood V_{A,R} of A in R.
- If I'' = I''_*, it is the deleted tubular neighbourhood V*_{A,R}. Here the star is taken relative to the structure induced on R as a subspace of D_{I'_0}, with the divisor induced by Θ_{d_0}.
- In the general case one has an intermediate stratum B (272):
  - A = D*_{I'_0 ⊔ I''} ⊂ closure(B), with B = D*_{I'_0 ⊔ I''_*} ⊂ closure(R), R = D_{I'_0};
  - the codimensions are d''_0 = card I''_0 and d''_* = card I''_*.

Next page. The corresponding topos V^{B(*)}_{A,R} is defined as the fibre product V_{A,R} ×_{V_{B,R}} V*_{B,R}. In words: points of R near A whose specialisation pattern is controlled by B, i.e. deleted along the B-direction only. This is then globalised to chains of codimensions d_* ⊃ d'_* ⊃ d''_* in M̄_{g,ν}. Grothendieck observes that the result depends only on (d_*, d'_0, d''_0).

In modern terms these are generalised homotopy links indexed by flags of strata A < B < R in a normal-crossings (toroidal) stratification. In the local model each is homotopy-equivalent to a torus (C*)^{k} times a contractible piece. They serve to glue the profinite/Teichmüller groupoid data along the boundary, giving the 'Lego' description of the Teichmüller tower near infinity.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The notation for stars and closures fluctuates: R is written D*_{I'_0} in the text but D_{I'_0} in (272). Grothendieck himself flags such star confusions on the next page ('attention aux *').
'immersion de codim I''' should read codim card I''.

ideas.what: Topoi of tubular and deleted tubular neighbourhoods V_{A,R}, V*_{A,R} of a stratum A inside a larger stratum R of a normal-crossings stratification, used to describe M_{g,ν} near infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy link / punctured tubular neighbourhood; in étale/topos form, Deligne's oriented products and vanishing topoi; the log/Kato–Nakayama boundary torus bundle.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Deligne/Laumon/Gabber (oriented products, vanishing topos, c. 1980s); Kato–Nakayama (1999) for log Betti realisations.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} and to the Teichmüller tower, but not to this formalism.

ideas.what: A 'relative' neighbourhood topos V^{B(*)}_{A,R} attached to a flag of strata A ⊂ closure(B) ⊂ closure(R), defined as a fibre product V_{A,R} ×_{V_{B,R}} V*_{B,R}, interpolating between V_{A,R} and V*_{A,R}.
ideas.modern_name: Generalised homotopy link of a flag of strata; the higher homotopy links in exit-path ∞-category theory.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn; Woolf (2009); Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s).

ideas.what: Indexing of strata of C^I by subsets J and decomposition of the codimension-d boundary into the disjoint union of the D_J with card J = d.
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. XIII (tame fundamental group near normal crossings), SGA 7.

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines neighbourhood topoi for whole flags of strata (A ⊂ B ⊂ R) by fibre products of tubular and deleted-tubular neighbourhood topoi. This anticipates the flag-indexed homotopy links of modern exit-path/stratified homotopy theory, specifically for the boundary of M̄_{g,ν]. The literature on the profinite Teichmüller tower near infinity (tangential base points, Lego game) works with neighbourhoods of single strata. It does not, to my knowledge, use these flag-indexed links or cite this formalism.
missed.quote: Le cas intermédiaire, "général", correspond bien à la donnée d'une strate intermédiaire entre A et R  A ⊂ B ⊂ R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Exit-path ∞-categories of M̄_{g,n} (and their profinite/étale versions) are of current interest, e.g. for Grothendieck–Teichmüller and moduli of curves with tangential base points. This page shows Grothendieck setting up exactly the combinatorial data such a theory needs. Historians could document it as an early instance.

missed.claim: The flag-topoi are only defined here, together with the conjecture-like remark (next page) that they depend only on (d_*, d'_0, d''_0). No computation or gluing theorem appears on this page.
missed.quote: NB ce topos ne dépend en fait que des d_*, d'_0, d''_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making this precise would give a stratified-topos (étale homotopy) presentation of M̄_{g,ν] near infinity. It could be compared with Kato–Nakayama spaces and with log étale fundamental groupoids.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a fairly routine setup of the local model, but it introduces flag-indexed (relative) tubular-neighbourhood topoi, essentially generalised homotopy links. These appear in the literature only later and independently. Interesting historically, but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: The equation numbers are (271) and (272), not (27') and (27'').
The label under A reads ("âme") — the 'soul' of the topos from the previous page — not ("image"). The label under R is illegible and is probably not "régénération".
Top-right marginal word: likely 'élémentaire' or similar, linked to 'topos élémentaire', rather than 'éliminations'.
Line 1 likely reads 'avec cette notation, l'âme du topos élémentaire envisagé est D*_{I\I'_1}', not 'l'image du type'.
In (272) the right-hand entry is D_{I'_0} without a star, consistent with R being the closed stratum.
